spans.title: The Sleeping Jury
spans.blurb: At the Clue Club, a judge watches the members around him slump into slumber, one by one, while the waiter calmly explains that this is not a mock trial.
spans.brokenNote: The text is cut off mid-sentence at the end ('or sprawled on the').

spans.title: Trial by Candlelight
spans.blurb: On Christmas Eve, by candlelight, a strange waiter puts a hanging judge on trial for the sentence of death, with the club's sleeping members as the stakes.

books.pairNote: The story restates the short's whole punch, that the waiter has drugged the members into a reversible lethargy, so reading it first defuses the short's apparent deaths.

spans.title: Pearls in the Lining
spans.blurb: Lady Moya's pearls have vanished from a locked dressing-room. Michael bets they never left it, and asks to see her wardrobe.

spans.title: The Red Lady of Toulouse
spans.blurb: An executioner and his crew celebrate too well the night before a morning's work in Toulouse. At three o'clock, the 'red lady' still waits to be assembled.

spans.title: The Thing by the Ruined Mill
spans.blurb: A rider takes a dark November road home. At the ruined mill his mare wheels in terror, and something cold and clammy strikes him in the face.

spans.title: The Missing Ticket Stub
spans.blurb: Caught slipping out of a theatre, a small-time crook swears he bought a ticket, if only he could find the stub. The Inspector waits, unimpressed.

spans.title: The Screaming Forest
spans.blurb: On an opal road between bright-green globes, a running figure is snatched by something that screams in triumph. The stranger watching from a cave has an axe.

spans.title: The Dragon in the Cave
spans.blurb: Peter calls three times at the cave mouth, sword thrust out, certain nothing will answer. Then comes a deep, deep sigh, and yards of bright green.

spans.title: The Dragon at the Window
spans.blurb: Tap, tap, tap at the nursery window: the dragon is back, warm as a stove, with room on his back for three children and more.

spans.title: Two Burglars, One Safe
spans.blurb: A burglar switches on his pocket light and finds another man already at the safe, masked, armed, and equally unwilling to introduce himself.

spans.title: Dreams from the Sea
spans.blurb: Each night Dean's dream grows: the green, shining place under the sea comes clearer, and the swimming shadows draw closer. His doctor writes a prescription for nerves.

spans.title: The Kiss in the Cave
spans.blurb: A cable from a far-travelling uncle warns Dean to leave the house above the sea at once. Instead he watches the moon rise, and sleeps, and dreams.
spans.spoilerNote: Depicts the kiss that sets the book's possession plot in motion, hinting at what is invading Dean before the book explains it.

spans.title: Stand and Deliver
spans.blurb: Two robbers stop a big, cheerful traveller on a forest road and demand his wallet. Simon has a cudgel, solid brawn, and nothing worth stealing but onions.

spans.title: Help, Ye Forest Powers
spans.blurb: A furious wood-nymph drags a lazy misanthrope on a headlong midnight run to a forest clearing, where a lone youth holds off a ring of robbers.
